introduction: Connecticut WIC offers nutrition and food support for eligible pregnant or postpartum participants and young children. An online Interest Form starts contact with a WIC worker.
description: Connecticut WIC offers nutrition and food support for eligible pregnant or postpartum participants and young children. An online Interest Form starts contact with a WIC worker.

sections.who: Applicants must live in Connecticut, meet income requirements and complete a nutrition assessment. Citizenship is not required. SNAP, TFA or HUSKY enrollment can establish income eligibility in the circumstances the program specifies.
sections.get: WIC provides food benefits through eWIC along with nutrition support. Clinic staff help identify the appropriate benefits and nutrition goals.
sections.docs:
• Identity and Connecticut address information.
  • Income or relevant SNAP, TFA or HUSKY enrollment records.
  • Information about pregnancy or the child’s health and feeding; confirm the clinic’s appointment checklist.
sections.apply:
1. Send an Interest Form or call

    Use the WIC Interest Form, or contact an office from the state’s local-agency list.

  2. Arrange the appointment

    A WIC worker will explain how to complete the application. Ask who should attend and which records to bring.

  3. Complete the nutrition assessment

    Discuss health, eating habits and nutrition questions with WIC staff before the eligibility decision.
sections.after: Follow the clinic’s food-list and eWIC instructions and keep future appointment dates.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using WIC application and screening; WIC overview. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Does the Interest Form enroll me?
No. A staff member follows up to complete the application.
Do I need proof of citizenship?
Connecticut WIC says citizenship or alien-status proof is not required.
Can SNAP or HUSKY help establish income eligibility?
Yes, under the program’s specified enrollment rules; the remaining WIC conditions still apply.
What happens at the nutrition assessment?
You discuss health and eating habits and any family nutrition questions with WIC staff.
